name: Dynatone

card.summary: A late-1960s handheld facial toning device that delivered mild electrical pulses to face muscles, marketed to smooth wrinkles and tighten the jaw and chin.
card.note: Historical device; modern microcurrent toners make similar claims.

quick.overview:
Dynatone was a handheld electric facial toner advertised in 1968 as a luxury device for toning the face. Like other mid-century devices, it sent mild pulses into facial muscles, which twitched, with the promise of firmer, younger-looking skin.

It is part of a lineage of electrical facial gadgets from 1930s facial irons to today's microcurrent toners.
quick.how: The user held the applicator against the face and moved it over the skin while the device pulsed. Similar contemporary devices, such as the Zeigler Electronic Facial Exerciser of about 1964, made muscles twitch under the applicator.
quick.risks: Electrical stimulation of the face carries risk of irritation, and published support for such devices is limited.

lead: Dynatone was a handheld facial toning device promoted in a 1968 newspaper advertisement as a luxury item retailing for about US$70, leaning more on advertising copy than science.

It belonged to a mid-century wave of electric beauty devices: the Zeigler Electronics Facial Exerciser (about 1964) used small shocks to twitch facial muscles, and electric masks and facial irons appeared in the 1930s [1]. Modern microcurrent and EMS facial toners market similar goals.

chain: Handheld device pulses current into face muscles
angle.text: Users were told that stimulating the facial muscles would firm and lift the face and reduce wrinkles and a soft chin.

paras: A 1968 newspaper advertisement presented Dynatone as a luxury toning device. A museum record catalogues a similar Zeigler Facial Exerciser (model Y-4), about 1964, under quack medicine [1]. In 1933 an electric face-moulding mask with heating coils was introduced to smooth wrinkles [2].
